sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Project settings and task commands
sections.what: Lists the app's name and version, the libraries it needs, and the commands a developer runs. The dev command starts a local preview server on 127.0.0.1 port 5173, build checks types and packages the app, test runs the tests once, and lint checks code style with zero warnings allowed.
sections.why: Likely reason: npm reads this file to install the right libraries and to know which commands exist.
sections.watch_out: Versions are pinned exactly with no ranges, so upgrading any library means editing this file on purpose, and Node 22.12 or newer is required.

summary: The frontend's package list. It names the app version 0.2.1, defines the commands such as dev, build, test, typecheck, and lint, and lists the exact library versions it uses.
purpose: Tells npm which libraries to install and which commands the task runner can call.
why: Likely reason: exact version numbers make installs repeat the same way on every machine.
how: npm reads this file during install, uses the lock file for exact versions, and runs a named script when asked.
inputs: The package registry during installs. The lock file for exact versions.
outputs: The node_modules folder and the built frontend files through the build script.
risks: Changing a pinned version without updating the lock file breaks installs. The Node version requirement must match the Replit and local setups.
debug: If npm ci fails, check that package.json and package-lock.json agree. If an install fails on version, check the Node version.
